chiefComplaint: chief complaint: the main reason for the visit
oct: optical coherence tomography (a scan of the retina and optic nerve)
gonio: gonioscopy: a look at the eye's drainage angle
cn5: cranial nerve V (trigeminal): feeling in the face
cn7: cranial nerve VII (facial): the muscles of the face
mrd: margin reflex distance: lid margin to the light reflex on the cornea
lf: levator function: how far the upper lid lifts, in mm
kp: keratic precipitates (inflammatory deposits on the back of the cornea)
pi: peripheral iridotomy (a laser opening in the iris)
nvi: neovascularization of the iris (new abnormal vessels)
ns: nuclear sclerosis (a cataract in the centre of the lens)
nvd: neovascularization of the disc (new abnormal vessels on the optic nerve)
nve: neovascularization elsewhere (new abnormal vessels in the retina)
cd: cup-to-disc ratio (size of the optic nerve cup)
trace: trace: barely there, less than grade 1
sc: without correction (sine correctione): no glasses or contact lenses
cc: with correction (cum correctione): with glasses or contact lenses
ph: pinhole: the best the eye can see through a pinhole
mr: manifest refraction (the patient chooses the clearest lenses)
pam: potential acuity meter (vision the eye could reach past a cataract)
jaeger: Jaeger near-vision chart (J1 is the smallest print)
snellen: Snellen acuity: test distance / distance at which a normal eye reads that line (20/20 is normal)
logmar: logMAR: log of the minimum angle of resolution (0.0 = 20/20; lower is better)
w: current glasses (what the patient wears now)
sph: sphere: the main lens power, in dioptres
cyl: cylinder: the astigmatism power, in dioptres
axis: axis: the direction of the cylinder, 1 to 180 degrees
add: near addition: extra plus power for reading
prism: prism: bends light so the eyes line up, in prism dioptres
base: base: which way the thick edge of the prism points (in, out, up, down)
pd: pupillary distance: between the centres of the pupils, in mm
dioptre: dioptre: the unit of lens power
prismDioptre: prism dioptre: the unit of prism power
dia: diameter of the contact lens, in mm
mmhg: millimetres of mercury (the unit of eye pressure)
apd: afferent pupillary defect (a weak pupil response from one optic nerve)
rapd: relative afferent pupillary defect (Marcus Gunn pupil)
dil: dilation: drops that widen the pupils
dv: ductions and versions: eye movements, each eye alone and both together
npa: near point of accommodation: closest distance print stays clear
npc: near point of convergence: closest distance the eyes can keep one image
e: esophoria: a latent inward turn, held straight by fusion
eIntermittent: intermittent esotropia: an inward turn that comes and goes
x: exophoria: a latent outward turn, held straight by fusion
xIntermittent: intermittent exotropia: an outward turn that comes and goes
rht: right hypertropia: the right eye is higher
lht: left hypertropia: the left eye is higher
poh: past ocular history: earlier eye diagnoses
pmh: past medical history: general health conditions
pmsfh: past medical, surgical, family and social history
cpt: Current Procedural Terminology: US codes for procedures and visits
icd: International Classification of Diseases: diagnosis codes
eyeCodes: eye exam codes (CPT 92002 to 92014), for a medical eye examination
emCodes: evaluation and management codes (CPT 99202 to 99215), graded by medical decision making or time
em: evaluation and management (an office visit code)
baseCurve: base curve: how steeply the back of the contact lens curves, in mm
vertex: vertex distance: from the back of the lens to the eye, in mm
slabOff: slab-off: prism ground into one lens so both eyes line up when reading
